model_annotations.Bulgarian: Диаграмата илюстрира сравнението на перплекситета (Perplexity) за две модели, означени като „Per-Output“ и „Per-Layer“, при различни стойности на спарситетния процент (Sparsity Rate). По хоризонталната ос са представени стойностите на спарситетния процент, които се променят от 10% до 80% с интервал от 10%, а по вертикалната ос е изобразен перплекситетът на логаритмична скала, която обхваща диапазон от 1 до 1000 (10⁰ до 10³). Стойностите по вертикалната ос са означени с логаритмична скала, като се използват маркери на 10⁰, 10¹, 10² и 10³. Всяка стойност на спарситетния процент съответства на група от два стълба – синият стълб представлява перплекситета за „Per-Output“, а оранжевият – за „Per-Layer“. Стълбовете са групирани по спарситетния процент и са разположени в ред, определен от увеличаването на спарситетния процент от ляво на дясно. Всички стълбове са изобразени с равни размери и без допълнителни визуални подчертавания, като различните групи са различими чрез цветовете и легендата в горния ляв ъгъл на диаграмата.
model_annotations.Chinese: The bar chart compares the perplexity of two models, Per-Output and Per-Layer, across different sparsity rates ranging from 10% to 80%. The horizontal axis represents the sparsity rate, with categories labeled as 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%, arranged in ascending order. The vertical axis, labeled "Perplexity," uses a logarithmic scale with values ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10³ (1000), marked at intervals of 10¹ (10), 10² (100), and 10³ (1000). Each sparsity rate category contains two adjacent bars: a blue bar representing Per-Output and an orange bar representing Per-Layer. For sparsity rates of 10% through 50%, both models exhibit low perplexity values, with Per-Output (blue) and Per-Layer (orange) bars having similar heights, both below 10. At 60% sparsity, the perplexity for both models increases slightly, with Per-Output at approximately 8 and Per-Layer at about 9. At 70% sparsity, the perplexity for both models rises further, with Per-Output at approximately 18 and Per-Layer at about 28. At 80% sparsity, the perplexity for both models increases significantly, with Per-Output reaching approximately 750 and Per-Layer reaching approximately 900. The legend in the top-left corner identifies the blue bars as "Per-Output" and the orange bars as "Per-Layer." The chart shows that the perplexity for both models generally increases with higher sparsity rates, with Per-Layer consistently having higher perplexity than Per-Output at each sparsity level.
model_annotations.English: The bar chart illustrates the perlexity of two different models, Per-Output and Per-Layer, across various sparsity rates ranging from 10% to 80%. The x-axis represents the sparsity rate, with values labeled at 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%. The y-axis represents perlexity, plotted on a logarithmic scale that ranges from 10^0 (1) to 10^3 (1000), with major gridlines at 10^1 (10) and 10^2 (100). For each sparsity rate, two bars are displayed side-by-side: a blue bar for Per-Output and an orange bar for Per-Layer. At sparsity rates of 10%, 20%, and 30%, both models exhibit low perlexity values, with the Per-Output model (blue) having a slightly lower perlexity than the Per-Layer model (orange). At 40% and 50% sparsity, the perlexity for both models increases slightly, with the Per-Layer model showing a slightly higher perlexity than the Per-Output model. At 60% sparsity, the perlexity for both models increases further, with the Per-Layer model again having a higher perlexity. At 70% sparsity, the perlexity for both models increases significantly, with the Per-Layer model showing a higher perlexity. At 80% sparsity, the perlexity for both models reaches its peak, with the Per-Layer model exhibiting a perlexity of approximately 1000, while the Per-Output model has a perlexity of approximately 500. The chart shows a clear trend of increasing perlexity with increasing sparsity rate for both models, with the Per-Layer model consistently having a higher perlexity than the Per-Output model across all sparsity rates.
model_annotations.German: Das Balkendiagramm visualisiert die Beziehung zwischen der Sparsitätsrate und der Komplexität, wobei die Komplexität auf einer logarithmischen Skala in der vertikalen Achse dargestellt ist und die Sparsitätsrate in Prozent auf der horizontalen Achse angegeben ist. Die horizontale Achse umfasst acht Kategorien mit Sparsitätsraten von 10% bis 80% in 10%-Schritten und ist alphabetisch sortiert. Die vertikale Achse, beschriftet mit „Perplexity“, reicht von 10⁰ bis 10³ und ist logarithmisch skaliert, mit sichtbaren Gitterlinien bei 10¹ und 10². Für jede Sparsitätsrate sind zwei gruppierte Balken dargestellt: ein blauer Balken, der „Per-Output“ repräsentiert, und ein orangefarbener Balken, der „Per-Layer“ darstellt. Die Balken sind nebeneinander angeordnet, wobei der blaue Balken links und der orangefarbene rechts positioniert ist. Die Höhe der Balken variiert mit der Sparsitätsrate: bei 10% sind beide Balken sehr niedrig, bei 80% sind die Balken am höchsten, wobei der orangefarbene Balken höher ist als der blaue. Die Farben der Balken werden in einer Legende oben links erklärt, die die Zuordnung von Farbe zu Kategorie spezifiziert. Es gibt keine visuellen Hervorhebungen wie Schattierungen oder Umrandungen.
